title: Free energy of melting against temperature
caption: For ice → water, ΔG = ΔH − TΔS = 6.01 − 0.022 T (kJ mol⁻¹). Below T = ΔH/ΔS = 6010/22 = 273 K, ΔG > 0 and melting does not happen on its own; above it ΔG < 0. At ΔG = 0 the two phases are in equilibrium: the melting point, 273 K.
alt: Graph of ΔG against temperature: a straight line falling from 6.01 kJ per mole at 0 K through zero at 273 K.
description: The horizontal axis is temperature in kelvin, the vertical axis ΔG for melting in kJ mol⁻¹.
ΔG = ΔH − TΔS is a straight line of gradient −ΔS = −0.022 kJ mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, starting at ΔH = +6.01 kJ mol⁻¹.
It crosses zero at T = 273 K: ice and water coexist. Left of this ice is stable, right of it water is.
